case_name: Rampukar Rai and Others v State of Bihar
respondent:
State of Bihar
Supreme Court of India

10 February 1993
Cr.A. No. 359 of 1992 (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 12 April 1990 of the Patna High Court in Cr. A. Nos. 128 and 228 of 1987)
The Judgment was delivered by: KULDIP SINGH, J.
1.  Ram Agya Rai and seven
facts: Ram Agya Rai and seven others were charged with the murder of Radhey Shyam Rai and were tried for the offences under Sections 302/149, 148, 147 Indian Penal Code and Section 27 of the Arms Act.
Ram Agya Rai was convicted under Sections 302 IPC, 148 IPC and was sentenced to imprisonment for life.
He was also sentenced to two years under Section 27 of the Arms Act.
All other accused were sentenced to life imprisonment under Section 302/149 Indian Penal Code.
Accused Ram Agya Rai, Parashu Rai, Ram Pukar Rai, Sheo Murat Rai and Nand Jee Rai were further convicted under Section 148 IPC and were sentenced to two years' rigorous imprisonment each.
Accused Bigan Rai, Deonagar Rai and Nathuni Kahar were further convicted under Section 147 IPC and were sentenced to one year rigorous imprisonment each.
issues: Whether the appellants were involved in the murder of Radhey Shyam Rai
Whether the prosecution had proved its case beyond reasonable doubt
petitioner_arguments: The statement of Ram Bachan Rai that his brother told him on way to hospital that the gunshot which injured him was fired by Ram Agya Rai, was totally false.
Ram Bachan Rai is not a reliable witness
In the presence of deceased at the Khalian there was no necessity of another person to be there to guard the paddy
respondent_arguments: PW 9 Ram Bachan Rai, the informant, is the only eyewitness to the occurrence
There was previous enmity between these witnesses and the accused party
court_reasoning: We are not inclined to rule out the presence of Ram Bachan Rai at the place of occurrence but we are of the view that his testimony has to be accepted with utmost scrutiny and caution
So far as PW 3 Paras Nath Singh and PW 7 Ram Jee Rai are concerned, the story put forward by them does not inspire confidence
It is difficult to believe that the appellants were accompanying Ram Agya Rai to commit the murder and still restrained themselves from using their respective weapons
holding: We give benefit of doubt to the appellants.
We allow the appeal, set aside the conviction and sentence of the appellants on all the counts and acquit them.
We direct that they be released forthwith.
